papers.study: Hoque KM, Halperin Kuhns VL, et al. (2020)
papers.title: The ABCG2 Q141K hyperuricemia and gout associated variant illuminates the physiology of human urate excretion
papers.verification_tier: Primary full text verified through Europe PMC XML on 2026-07-27.

full_text_extract.method: Q140K mouse model; jejunal and renal Western blots, intestinal immunofluorescence, and intestinal-loop urate-flux measurements.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: Q140K+/+ jejunal ABCG2 protein abundance was 78% lower than WT by Western blot.
The article's like-for-like Western-blot comparison was 78% jejunal reduction versus 44% renal reduction.
Male Q140K+/+ fractional excretion of urate was 47% lower.
exact_quantitative_findings.details: n=12; p=0.01. Female mice showed no change; n=7; p=0.6263.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: Modeled ABCG2-mediated jejunal urate flux was reduced 84.2% in Q140K+/+ mice.

abstract_vs_fulltext_difference: Primary-text verification confirms 78% jejunal versus 44% renal loss as the like-for-like Western-blot comparison.

The article HTML/XML, version-of-record PDF, supplementary-information PDF, and publisher source-data workbook contain no 53% or 88% intestinal reduction. The older 53%/88% sentence entered COMP-016 as an explicitly unverified search-summary claim and was then mislabeled as a verbatim snippet in the historical COMP-017 output; it is not a primary-source quotation.

The primary article separately reports a 78% Western-blot reduction and a statistically significant reduction in jejunal immunofluorescence signal. These are distinct measurements and are not combined into a new percentage.
scope_notes: This is Q140K disease-state mouse evidence, not a healthy-human baseline estimate.
The paper does not test clomiphene or establish direct androgen-receptor repression of intestinal ABCG2.

papers.study: Liu L, Zhao T, Shan L, Cao L, Zhu X, Xue Y (2021)
papers.title: Estradiol regulates intestinal ABCG2 to promote urate excretion via the PI3K/Akt pathway
papers.verification_tier: Primary full text verified through Europe PMC XML on 2026-07-27.

full_text_extract.method: Caco-2 concentration/time experiments with estradiol benzoate and LY294002. The paper also contains clinical and mouse work, but those claims are not rendered by this audit.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: Caco-2 cells were exposed to 10^-4, 10^-6, and 10^-8 mol/L estradiol benzoate for 24, 48, or 72 hours.
10^-4 mol/L (100 µM) estradiol benzoate significantly increased ABCG2 mRNA at 48 hours without a dose-dependent effect.
50 µM LY294002 partially blocked the 100 µM estradiol-benzoate effect on ABCG2 mRNA.

abstract_vs_fulltext_difference: The primary text fixes the Caco-2 active condition at a nominal 100 µM and shows that the tested response was not dose-dependent.
That cell-culture condition supports a pharmacological in-vitro mechanism; it does not quantify physiological intestinal regulation.
scope_notes: The retained Caco-2 findings are In Vitro evidence. The paper's clinical and mouse evidence contexts are not rendered, and this record does not answer the healthy-human sex-stratified baseline question.

papers.study: Slepnev AA, Abalenikhina YV, Popova NM, Shchulkin AV, Yakusheva EN (2023)
papers.title: Effect of Sex Hormones on the ABCG2 Transport Protein in Caco-2 Cells
papers.journal: Biochemistry (Moscow), Supplement Series A: Membrane and Cell Biology
papers.verification_tier: Official publisher-supplied English abstract and journal metadata verified on 2026-07-27; full numerical results were not extracted.

full_text_extract.method: Caco-2 cells; Western-blot ABCG2 measurement after 24-hour exposure to progesterone, estradiol, or testosterone at nominal 1, 10, or 100 µM; orphan-receptor inhibitor conditions.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: All three hormones increased ABCG2 at all three nominal concentrations tested.
exact_quantitative_findings.details: The minimum tested active concentration was 1 µM; fold changes were not extracted.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: PXR and FXR inhibition reduced the testosterone-associated increase, but ABCG2 remained above control.
CAR and PXR inhibition reduced the estradiol-associated increase, while PXR and FXR inhibition prevented the progesterone-associated increase.

abstract_vs_fulltext_difference: The correct attribution is Slepnev et al., not Klyushova et al.

The publisher abstract supports nominal 1, 10, and 100 µM culture conditions and PXR/FXR involvement. It does not establish free-tissue exposure or justify a serum-total or serum-free testosterone multiplier.
scope_notes: This In Vitro result does not support direct androgen-receptor repression; androgen-receptor involvement was not itself excluded by the reported inhibitor design.
It does not establish a physiological testosterone effect, clomiphene mechanism, or human intestinal urate-flux effect.

papers.study: MacLean C, Moenning U, Reichel A, Fricker G (2008)
papers.title: Closing the gaps: a full scan of the intestinal expression of P-glycoprotein, breast cancer resistance protein, and multidrug resistance-associated protein 2 in male and female rats
papers.verification_tier: Primary PubMed abstract verified on 2026-07-27; no effect-size estimate was available in the abstract.

full_text_extract.method: Male and female rats; qRT-PCR and Western blot across duodenum, jejunum, ileum, colon, and a complete 3-cm segmentation of the intestine.

exact_quantitative_findings.finding: The authors reported that no sex-specific differences were observed for the intestinal transporter-expression scan.

abstract_vs_fulltext_difference: The verified abstract supports a qualitative healthy-rat null across the studied intestinal scan.
It supplies neither a healthy-human estimate nor a quantified human population threshold test.
scope_notes: This is Animal Model evidence and cannot resolve healthy-human intestinal ABCG2 sex stratification.

cross_paper_synthesis.direct_human_baseline: UNRESOLVED: no sex-stratified GTEx intestinal distribution or HPA intestinal protein values were extracted.
cross_paper_synthesis.qualitative_prior: The sources do not establish a large healthy-baseline human intestinal sex difference. Rat baseline, Q140K mouse disease-state, and pharmacological Caco-2 findings remain separate evidence contexts.
forbidden_inferences: physiological hormone regulation magnitude from nominal high-concentration culture exposure
Q141K-conditioned response ordering for gut-lumen uricase

evidence_boundaries.question: Healthy-human baseline intestinal ABCG2 sex difference
evidence_boundaries.boundary: No direct GTEx/HPA sex-stratified intestinal values were extracted and the 1.5-fold threshold was not tested.

evidence_boundaries.question: Healthy-rat baseline intestinal ABCG2 sex difference
evidence_boundaries.boundary: MacLean et al. 2008 reported no sex-specific difference in the rat intestinal transporter-expression scan. This does not estimate a healthy-human effect.

evidence_boundaries.question: Q140K disease-state sex interaction
evidence_boundaries.boundary: Hoque et al. 2020 reported sex-dependent urate phenotypes in Q140K mice. The verified like-for-like Western comparison is 78% jejunal versus 44% renal reduction; the prior 88% value is not retained.

evidence_boundaries.question: Direct androgen-receptor repression of intestinal ABCG2
evidence_boundaries.boundary: Slepnev et al. 2023 reported increased Caco-2 ABCG2 after nominal 1, 10, and 100 µM testosterone and implicated PXR/FXR with inhibitor conditions. AR was not tested or excluded, and no serum-total or serum-free multiplier is emitted.

evidence_boundaries.question: Clomiphene, intervention selection, or uricase response
evidence_boundaries.boundary: COMP-017 did not test clomiphene, select an intervention, or estimate Q141K-conditioned response to a gut-lumen uricase.
